description: REQ-001 (behavioral-spec.md lines 67-71) explicitly documents an edge case: 'caller invoked with no ANICCA_HOME set at all... if the CALLER did not set ANICCA_HOME, this requirement does not apply -- whatever $HOME/.openclaw/.env/$HOME/.hermes/.env set (or leave unset) passes through unchanged, matching pre-fix behavior for that case.' The fix's own bash logic (`[ -n "$_ANICCA_HOME_CALLER" ] && ANICCA_HOME="$_ANICCA_HOME_CALLER"`) is written to special-case exactly this branch (when the caller's ANICCA_HOME was empty, the restore-assignment is skipped). Yet skills/self/spawn/lib/__tests__/run-sh-anicca-home-preservation.test.mjs contains only 2 test cases, and BOTH set `ANICCA_HOME: callerAniccaHome` in the spawned env -- neither test omits ANICCA_HOME from the caller's env. This is a documented, spec-mandated edge case with zero test coverage; a regression that broke this specific conditional branch (e.g. reversing the `-n` to `-z`, or always overwriting) would not be caught by either existing test.

evidence.snippet: test("run.sh preserves the CALLER's ANICCA_HOME across $HOME/.openclaw/.env sourcing...", () => {...env: { HOME: home, ANICCA_HOME: callerAniccaHome, PATH: ... }...}); // and the second test case (line 101-139) also always sets ANICCA_HOME -- no case ever omits it
